patch.value: Metric series live in item history, never in an item body

A run emits a monotonically growing series of metric events. Written to an item body, which is a scalar field, two concurrent writers produce a genuine conflict on every write, and a conflicted body is unparseable. Written to the append-only history stream, both sides' events survive a merge as their union, which pm-vcs proved empirically against a real git merge rather than by assumption. This single rule is what makes concurrent sweeps merge cleanly, so it is a constraint on every command that records a metric, not a convention.
No command writes a metric value to an item body or any scalar field; a test merges two branches that both logged to one run and asserts the union of events with zero conflicts and zero loss

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Decision reconfirmed against the shipped host rather than against the earlier spec note: pm append targets the body, so any command that used it for metrics would conflict on every concurrent write. The rule holds and now has a named counterexample attached to it.
